correctness.rationale: The event that the prescribed pair is a concept splits into disjoint incidence-block constraints; its probability is exactly p^(ab)(1-p^a)^N(1-p^b)^(r-a). Conditional outside-intent column patterns over the extent are independent Bernoulli columns truncated to exclude the all-one vector. For any extent subset X, this yields [(1-p^|X|)/(1-p^a)]^N. Pairwise inclusion-exclusion gives the second moment. A uniform random extent subset has fair-binomial size. Sandwiching intent preservation above and below log_(1/p)N with a width O(log a) and applying binomial anti-concentration proves the uniform L1 error O(log a/sqrt a); Berry–Esseen completes the Gaussian bound. Every step uses p fixed in (0,1), 1<=a<=r,1<=b<m. The self-contained code was executed and gave VERIFY_OK for 264 fully enumerated rational-weighted instances, including conditional variance. Finite computations corroborate exact identities, not the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The complete finite conditional probability reduction and the uniform Gaussian concentration of the random stability index are not stated or implied by the inspected primary results on deterministic stability computation, empirical sample-resampling, or expected concept counts. In particular, exact algorithmic evaluation for an arbitrary supplied matrix does not give the conditional distribution or its growing-size limit; empirical convergence of stability across datasets is not the same statement. Searches of accessible published mathematical records gave no covering statement. This is a best-knowledge comparison, not a proof of global priority; incomplete 2022/2015 full-text comparisons are residual risks.

value.rationale: Concept stability measures robustness of a Galois-closed intent to deletion of object witnesses and is a standard computationally demanding concept-lattice invariant. The exact conditional moments and especially a uniform quantitative Gaussian crossover determine a natural probabilistic phase boundary for prescribed concepts: stability changes from near one to near zero as outside-intent attributes cross the square-root-width critical scale. The independence from the number of other objects and from intent cardinality is structural, allowing the law to be used across differently sized finite contexts. This is not a mere normalization or one finite table; its claim covers an infinite family with a precise error bound. Limitation: it is conditional, not a typicality theorem for a uniformly sampled concept.
